The test image shows corn stalks split open with:
- A middle stalk with **jet-black to dark exterior** with mottled yellow-green coloring — very distinctive shiny/glazed appearance
- Shredded, fibrous internal pith tissue
- Straw-colored/bleached outer rind on surrounding stalks
- Small black specks visible on surfaces

This strongly suggests a stalk rot. Top candidates: **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** (jet-black exterior), **Charcoal_stalk_rot** (black microsclerotia in pith), **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (black pycnidia on rind).

Let me view reference images for the top 3 candidates simultaneously.

The reference images confirm:
- **Anthracnose_stalk_rot**: Shows shiny jet-black exterior stalk discoloration AND shredded fibrous pith with black flecks — matches the test image very well
- **Charcoal_stalk_rot**: Fibrous shredded pith but straw-yellow rind, no distinctive black exterior
- **Diplodia_stalk_rot**: Brown/tan exterior with dark node discoloration, not jet-black

Let me view 3 more references to meet the minimum requirement and rule out any others.

All 6 references viewed. Analysis complete.

**Key comparison:**

| Feature | Test Image | Anthracnose_stalk_rot | Charcoal_stalk_rot | Diplodia_stalk_rot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jet-black shiny exterior | ✅ Yes (middle stalk) | ✅ Yes (hallmark) | ❌ Straw-yellow | ❌ Tan-brown |
| Shredded fibrous pith | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| Black specks in pith | ✅ Yes | ✅ Microsclerotia | ✅ Microsclerotia | ❌ Pycnidia on rind |

The **shiny, jet-black exterior** on the middle stalk with yellow-green mottling is the defining characteristic. The Anthracnose_stalk_rot reference shows exactly this — glazed dark exterior plus fibrous shredded pith with black flecks. Charcoal and Diplodia do not show this black exterior discoloration. Physoderma shows localized node rotting with brown coloring, not jet-black. Fusarium affects ears primarily.

This glazed, jet-black exterior is the primary distinguishing feature not seen in Charcoal stalk rot (straw-yellow rind) or Diplodia stalk rot (tan-brown exterior with pycnidia on rind surface)."}
